description: Cases the worker's prompt broker must pass over its real endpoint. crates/paneflow-serve/tests/prompt_conformance.rs runs every case with plain protocol clients against a real paneflow serve worker on a per-process endpoint, with no display; a case listed here with no runner is a failure, not a skip.

cases.summary: With two followers and one prompt, the first prompt.reply gives the asker {status: answered, answer}, the second follower receives ended with reason answered, and a late reply from it is refused with -32060 and data {reason: not_pending}.
With two followers, a reply with cancel = true gives the asker cancelled and the other follower receives ended with reason cancelled.
With one follower that shows input only, a pick request returns unsupported at once and queues nothing.
When one of two followers disconnects, the prompt stays pending and the remaining follower can still answer it.
Three prompts requested in order reach a follower that connects afterwards as three requested frames, oldest first, after a following header that counts them.
A prompt requested with no follower returns no_client and queues nothing; a prompt pending when its only follower disconnects ends with no_client for the asker.
A request whose wait_ms passes returns {status: pending, id}; prompt.wait on that id returns the answer once a follower replies.
A pick with two items sharing an id, a request with no title, or allow_other with multiple is refused with -32602 naming the field.
With 16 prompts pending, another request returns busy.
A prompt with timeout 1 that nobody answers ends with timeout for the asker, and every follower receives ended with reason timeout.
A worker that stops while an asker waits gives it failed with a detail saying the worker stopped.

Three prompt.request calls with origin {kind: agent, session} are queued; a fourth from the same session within the second returns {status: rate_limited} and no follower receives a requested frame for it, while another session is still admitted.

A prompt whose origin is an agent reaches a follower outside every pane with a token of 128 bits; prompt.reply without that token, or with another, is refused with -32060 and data {reason: not_pending}, the refusal an unknown id gets, the prompt stays pending, and a reply with the token is accepted.

A caller running in a pane follows prompts and is given neither the agent's prompt nor a token for it; its prompt.reply carrying the token another follower received is refused with -32060 and data {reason: not_pending}, and the prompt stays pending for the client outside every pane.
